answer: Faking thousands of identities means fronting real value across all of them, and slashing burns it on provable misbehavior. Sybil resistance can come from bonding identity to slow, costly capital: each agent must lock a jade-token stake that vests over months, with withdrawals throttled like meltwater from a glacier. Honest agents recover stake steadily, turning reputation into an oasis of trust that copycat swarms cannot cheaply counterfeit. From once0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
